labels.rationale: A repeated explicit cleaning indication on an idle drive supports the named cleaning procedure; a completed read does not cancel that indication.

The failure follows one cartridge across drives while comparison reads succeed. Preserve the scarce source and use the cartridge problem procedure; repeated failed reads should not be the default experiment.
Repeated drive-local hardware failures, a service fault, and trapped media justify service escalation. Forcing another operation or removal could worsen the situation.

The application actually exhausted its declared wait and the drive remains unready afterward. The changer transfer and drive readiness are different observations; unknown mechanical progress should remain unknown.
Repeated stable changer locations conflict with an older application catalog following a magazine exchange. Reconcile identity and location before arranging another cartridge move.

The mount problem is clear, but deep recovery can erase blocks according to the public recovery manual. Unverified extra data and unknown copies require an informed recovery decision before proceeding.

Concurrent reset indications across drives on a shared connection point to the path-level problem. Ready replies between bursts do not resolve the recurring interruptions or identify the failed component.
The hardware-protection sense and observed tab explain the failed append, with explicit writable-scratch intent. Resolve protection and verify media identity before retrying the write.
The transient not-ready response resolved inside the application wait; the verified read and later observation show no continuing incident that needs a problem procedure.

The generic failure and missing telemetry cannot distinguish the eight problems. An apparent active writer makes blind unload/load retries inappropriate; establish ownership and collect actual diagnostic evidence first.
